content:
Class 8 opens quietly. Rational numbers look like last year’s work. Then the paper asks WHICH property was used in a step. Or it wants three rationals between −1/2 and −1/3. That is where prepared students pull ahead. Below sits a free IMO Class 8 Rational Numbers online test — 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation under every answer. Eight out of ten is the score to beat.

What the IMO asks from Rational Numbers in Class 8

  • Standard form and equivalent rational numbers.
  • The properties by name: closure, commutative, associative, distributive.
  • Additive inverses, reciprocals, and the roles of 0 and 1.
  • Rational numbers between two given numbers.
  • Number-line work and multi-step word problems.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • The average (a + b)/2 always sits between a and b. It is the fastest "find one between" tool.
  • The reciprocal of a negative rational stays negative. Zero has no reciprocal at all.
  • Spot the shortcut: 7/9 × 5/13 + 7/9 × 8/13 = 7/9 × (5/13 + 8/13) = 7/9.
  • Standard form needs a POSITIVE denominator in lowest terms. So 48/−60 becomes −4/5.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Ranking negatives by digit size. −5/6 is SMALLER than −2/3, not bigger.
  • Leaving a minus sign in the denominator of a final answer.
  • Mixing up the additive inverse (−x) with the reciprocal (1/x).

questions.q: Arrange the following rational numbers in ascending order: -3/5, -7/10, -1/2
questions.explanation: Convert all to denominator 10: -3/5 = -6/10, -7/10 = -7/10, -1/2 = -5/10. Comparing: -7/10 < -6/10 < -5/10 (further left on the number line = smaller). So ascending order: -7/10, -3/5, -1/2.

questions.q: For two rational numbers a/b and c/d where b > 0 and d > 0, if a/b < c/d, which of the following MUST be true?
questions.explanation: Since b > 0 and d > 0, multiply both sides of a/b 6 + 2 = 8. Option D fails when a = 0 or signs vary.

questions.q: If a, b, c are rational numbers on a number line with a < b < c, and b - a = c - b, then b equals:
questions.explanation: From b - a = c - b, add b to both sides and add a: 2b = a + c, so b = (a + c)/2. This is the arithmetic mean of a and c. The condition b - a = c - b means b is equally spaced between a and c.

questions.q: How many rational numbers exist between 1/5 and 2/5?

questions.q: If x is a rational number such that -2/3 < x < -1/2, which of the following MUST be true about x²?
questions.explanation: From -2/3 < x < -1/2, take absolute values (reversing because x is negative): 1/2 < |x| < 2/3. Squaring all parts (all positive, so inequality preserved): (1/2)² < x² < (2/3)², giving 1/4 < x² < 4/9.
